original_question: For a compact Hermitian manifold (X, omega), define cap(X, omega) as the infimum of integral_X (omega + dd^c phi)^n over omega-plurisubharmonic functions phi with 0 <= phi <= 1. Relate this quantity to the geometry of (X, omega), determine whether it can be computed from geometric data, and determine how it behaves under deformations.
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Question 31 (Dinew–Kołodziej): the problem of relating the Hermitian capacity cap(X, ω) := inf{∫_X (ω + dd^cφ)^n : φ ∈ PSH(X, ω), 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1} to the geometry of the compact Hermitian manifold (X, ω), asking in particular whether it is computable from geometric data and how it behaves under deformations.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual question. It correctly identifies the ambient setting as a compact Hermitian manifold (X, ω), uses the same capacity-type quantity cap(X, ω) defined by infimizing the total Monge–Ampère mass ∫_X (ω + dd^cφ)^n over ω-plurisubharmonic functions with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, and asks for exactly the same three outputs as the paper: a relation to the geometry of (X, ω), computability from geometric data, and behavior under deformations.
missing_details: The paper is in the non-Kähler Hermitian setting: ω is the positive (1,1)-form of a Hermitian metric and is not assumed closed.
The exponent n should be identified explicitly as n = dim_C X.
The admissible functions are exactly φ ∈ PSH(X, ω), where this means ω + dd^cφ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents.
The bounds 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 are pointwise on X and are part of the definition, not an optional normalization.

The quantity is motivated by the preceding discussion that, in the Hermitian case, the total volume ∫_X (ω + dd^cφ)^n generally depends on φ; this nearby context explains why this capacity is being introduced.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should state that the deformation question concerns deformations of the Hermitian pair (X, ω), not an unspecified notion of deformation.
The paper does not ask for a full classification or an explicit formula in all cases; it asks to relate cap(X, ω) to geometry, and specifically asks whether it is computable from geometric data.
refined_question:
Let (X, ω) be a compact Hermitian manifold, where ω is the positive (1,1)-form of a Hermitian metric and n = dim_C X. Write PSH(X, ω) for the ω-plurisubharmonic functions, i.e. the upper-semicontinuous functions φ on X such that ω + dd^cφ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents. Define
cap(X, ω) := inf{∫_X (ω + dd^cφ)^n : φ ∈ PSH(X, ω), 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 on X}.
How is cap(X, ω) related to the geometry of the Hermitian pair (X, ω)? In particular, is cap(X, ω) computable in terms of geometric data of (X, ω), and how does it vary under deformations of the Hermitian manifold/form?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 4.1 of the paper, not the earlier Kähler questions. Question 31 introduces exactly the same quantity cap(X, ω) with the same infimum and the same constraint 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, and then asks exactly the same two follow-up issues: computability from geometric data and behavior under deformations. The nearby setup in Section 4 defines the Hermitian context and the meaning of ω-plurisubharmonicity, while Questions 29 and 30 explain the motivating phenomenon that in the Hermitian setting the total Monge–Ampère mass generally depends on φ. The paper does not state an equivalent reformulation of Question 31, so no alternate formulation should be introduced.
